newsitem.title: USA: INSIGHT-Dollar to take breather, then attack yen.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT-Dollar to take breather, then attack yen.

text.p: After setting a fresh 44-month high of 116.20 yen, the U.S. dollar is likely to consolidate before launching a new attack on the Japanese currency right after New Year, analysts said on Friday.
The dollar took out three resistance levels versus the yen in a row, climbing on Friday to its highest level since March 31, 1993, before retreating to close at 115.25.

Traders said Friday's action in thinning volume ahead of the pre-New Year weekend underscored the dollar's need to take a breather after a series of sharp upward moves against the yen, launched from Monday's low of 113.60.
Technicians stressed the dollar's upside will remain intact for as long as supports at 1.5510 marks, 114.80 yen and 1.3425 Swiss francs hold.
I.D.E.A. senior currency analyst Chris Turner expected the foreign exchange action to continue to revolve around the yen.

"It's a yen-led move because mark/yen is participating as well," Turner said of the mark/yen drive through key resistance at 74.40 -- or a 62-percent retracement of the slide from 75.90 to 72.05 -- to a session's high of 74.63.
The 74.10 mark/yen level was important also because it is where a rising trendline from the 1995 lows is coming in at.
Traders tied the mark/yen gains to the fact most markets in Europe were closed Wednesday and Thursday and market players had to make up for lost trading opportunities.
"Today's mark/yen rally was very strong. That may put a cap on dollar/mark," Turner explained. "Dollar/mark has been underperforming since the rally against the yen."
Sterling/yen was a winner, climbing to a four-year high while cable rose to $1.6945 -- its highest since October 1992.
"People are going to be long dollar until Japan's Ministry of Finance says there is a problem with a weak yen," added Turner who foresaw further pressure on the yen.
Turner, however, expected only "verbal intervention" and not actual yen buying by the Bank of Japan.

Analysts also noted the dollar/Swiss strength with the key 1.35 level in a 19-month bull channel giving way on Friday. They noted the futures contract for the Swiss franc fell to its lowest level since December 1994 -- which signaled further Swiss franc weakness ahead in the cash market.
Scott Siller, senior analyst at MCM CurrencyWatch saw dollar/yen "moving up to 117.30. Why not? Since 116.20 is the upper end of long-term bull channel from September 1995."
